tasks.short: Train workers in preparation, service and safety

steps.what: Identify worker training needs and select current food preparation and safety procedures
Train workers by demonstrating food preparation, service, sanitation and safety procedures
Observe practice, correct errors and confirm readiness for assigned food-service duties

tasks.design: Use current approved procedures in {DOCS} and keep demonstration, observed practice and readiness judgements with the supervisor. No generated procedure or automated competence score is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Competent food handling requires observed practical performance.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing procedure documents support consistent training without a new tool.
tasks.still_hard: Spot errors under actual service conditions and correct them clearly.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt instruction to the worker and verify real practice.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor retains training and readiness responsibility.

evidence.claim: Practical demonstration and observation remain necessary to judge whether a worker can apply a procedure.

assumptions: The business’s existing procedure owner supplies current approved instructions; that maintenance is unchanged.
Supervisor observes training needs in s1 and practice in s3; no structured competency feed is assumed.
Worker learning time remains unchanged outside focal supervisor labour. No new application creates incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which approved procedures and readiness standards apply
research_questions: Do workers demonstrate the procedure correctly after training without prompting?

incremental.description: No new training tool or process to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=20+55+25=100. Preparation, demonstration and observed practice retain effort; no learning time is treated as clerical savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check work requirements, staffing availability and restrictions for the current service
Assign duties, responsibilities and work stations to employees

tasks.design: Keep duty decisions and direct communication with the supervisor, using the existing roster in {HCM} and service board in {OPS_SYSTEM}. A demand forecast may inform requirements but does not assign individual workers in this design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments depend on current availability, competence and changing service conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Sales forecasting products exist, but their capability does not establish automatic individual allocation.
tasks.still_hard: Balance coverage, practical capability and fair assignments.
tasks.human_edge: Know when a worker needs support or a changed station.
tasks.altitude: Assignment authority remains with the supervisor.

reach.learn: Explain coverage needs and practical constraints

evidence.claim: Tenzo forecasts sales and managers adjust the forecast and schedule from it; this is not evidence of automated individual duty assignment.

assumptions: Supervisor checks actual availability and relevant restrictions in s1; no clean individual capability matrix is assumed.
Roster production and workers’ own service activity are unchanged outside this task.
No additional ranking, monitoring or allocation system is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Which skills and restrictions each workstation requires
research_questions: Which assignment changes happen during service and why?

incremental.description: No new allocation software or maintenance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=30+70=100. Availability checking and individual assignment retain time; no forecast benefit is imported into this task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Present bills and accept customer payments

steps.what: Check the customer order and identify the correct bill
Calculate the bill total using current prices and entered order items
Present bills and accept payments, handling cash or payment exceptions
outputs: completed payment or unresolved payment issue

tasks.design: Keep the existing {OTHER} restaurant point-of-sale system for arithmetic and payment recording. The supervisor checks the bill, presents it and handles the customer interaction; no new customer-payment mechanism is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cash, split bills and disputed charges need direct assistance.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing point-of-sale arithmetic is already part of today’s workflow.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve billing questions and failed tenders correctly.
tasks.human_edge: Explain charges and help the customer complete payment.
tasks.altitude: Billing and payment authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Check bill identity and tender status

evidence.claim: Restaurant point-of-sale systems already total entered orders; that existing automation is not a new human-labour saving.

assumptions: Servers or the supervisor create entered customer orders during the existing order-taking task; that capture time is unchanged outside this payment boundary. S1 includes checking identity and order correctness.
Restaurant management maintains configured prices under its existing process; missing or disputed items are clarified manually before payment.
The system step represents existing nonhuman processing, excluded from focal baseline. No new application or maintenance is introduced.
unknowns: Which billing exceptions and payment methods occur locally
research_questions: Which payment exceptions consume supervisor time after routine POS arithmetic is excluded?

incremental.description: No additional payment system or maintenance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Focal B=20+60=80; R=20+60=80, so gross and net saving are 0%. The existing system arithmetic share of 20 is not human labour and cannot create a new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Handle cash, prepare deposits and support payroll

steps.what: Count cash and verify deposit and payroll source records
Prepare deposit summaries and payroll input totals from verified records
Review financial totals, prepare physical deposits and submit approved payroll inputs

tasks.design: Use protected calculation fields in an existing {SPREADSHEET} or native {PAYROLL} input form to total verified records and prepare summaries. The supervisor still counts cash, resolves discrepancies, prepares the physical deposit and signs off the exact inputs; finance retains payment execution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated summation and copying between close sheets and payroll inputs adds clerical effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms and protected arithmetic can reuse captured numbers without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Cash discrepancies, missing time entries and approval limits.
tasks.human_edge: Investigate exceptions and preserve custody and accountability.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor prepares summaries with less repeated arithmetic, without gaining bank-transfer or payroll-release rights.

reach.learn: Provide verified hours and correction evidence

evidence.claim: Protected arithmetic and native input forms can reduce repeated financial summary preparation; this is an unmeasured design hypothesis.

assumptions: S1 produces dated denomination counts, counted_total, POS reference, employee_id, pay_period and verified_hours, including manual investigation of discrepancies; its full 40% remains. S2 includes capturing these values once and checking input units within its remaining 15 baseline units.

Workers create original time entries and POS records arise from existing transactions; their capture effort is unchanged outside this task. Missing time data or cash mismatches require manual resolution, never guessed values.
Finance supplies approved input formats and pay-period rules. Test existing close and payroll forms before new calculation work; no automatic banking or payroll execution is introduced.
Physical cash handling and deposit preparation remain fully counted in s1 and s3.
unknowns: How much summary arithmetic is already automated
Which payroll and deposit formats the organisation uses
research_questions: Does single entry reduce close preparation after cash checks, time verification and review are counted?

already_counted.description: Capture verified values and inspect calculated summaries
Approve totals and preserve physical deposit controls

incremental.description: Check changed input formats and report failed calculations
Maintain protected formulas, mappings and access

approvals.approved_version: Supervisor approves exact deposit summary and payroll input revisions, source references, period and recipients before handover; changed figures or recipients void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=40+15+35=90; gross=10%; minus 1 focal upkeep gives 9% net. Low: existing forms already calculate totals. High: only repeated summary arithmetic and copying shrink; capture, verification, cash handling and approval keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Supervisors can prepare financial summaries with less repeated arithmetic while retaining practical training, duty decisions and payment assistance.
reach: Submit clearer verified inputs to payroll staff
role.ambitious_version: Use reliable summaries to reduce clerical interruptions without expanding payment authority or automating worker judgement.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
